newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar in volatile trade.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar on Thursday in volatile trading, dealers said.
"The session opened with mild demand for the dollar and the U.S. currency rose to 3.558 shekels," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"Just as they were about to set the representative rate the trend changed and the business sector started converting dollars into shekels and the shekel rose sharply," she said.
The dollar representative rate was fixed at 3.5520 shekels but in subsequent trading the dollar was at 3.5440 shekels.

"Today's change may be the turning point at which the shekel starts to recover. Many players believe that there was no reason for the sharp depreciation of the shekel and that it will start rising in the near term," she said.
The shekel dropped as much as five percent in the last week of June after the government announced changes in the exchange rate mechanism and the Bank of Israel slashed interest rates.
The Israeli currency subsequently gained back part of its losses but is still lower against the dollar than before the depreciation began.

"In the long run I believe that the central bank will need to intervene again in the forex market to support the shekel," the dealer said, indicating he believed the currency would return to the edge of its trading band, where it was before mid-June.

The 3.5520 shekel representative rate for the dollar compared with 3.5560 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8238 against 3.8337 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0521 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0723 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9775 shekels compared with 1.9851 on Wednesday.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
